source_review.notes: Reviewed the GNU Emacs gap and marker manuals plus current buffer.c and insdel.c source, Finseth's MIT-hosted editor text, current Unicode segmentation and normalization annexes, Microsoft's VS Code text-buffer engineering account, and the Xi rope/text-engine documents. All ten final destinations returned HTTP 200.

evidence: Checked C, g0, g1, h, n, p, q, d, k, logical ranges, physical ranges, and half-open interval notation for consistent domains.
Checked the piecewise phys(i) mapping only applies to valid logical lookup indices and distinguishes insertion positions.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Element-transfer work is explicitly separated from byte traffic, allocation, metadata, I/O, rendering, synchronization, and latency.

evidence: Replayed the eight-slot trace from abcd through movement to position 2, insertion of X and Y, backspace, forward delete, movement to the end, and insertion of !.
Confirmed final text abXd!, logical length 5, gap [5,8), gap width 3, capacity 8, and exactly three moved slots.
Checked example mappings for C=8, g0=2, g1=5: h=3, n=5, phys(1)=1, and phys(2)=5.
numerical_recomputation.notes: Finite counts validate the stated examples, not arbitrary workload complexity or runtime latency.

evidence: Derived n=C-(g1-g0) from the two live extents g0 and C-g1.
Checked that left and right movement preserve constant gap width because both boundaries change equally.
Re-derived per-edit modeled work Theta(d+k) without growth, Theta(d+k+n) with full transfer growth, and sequence movement sum |p_t-p_(t-1)|.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: The bounds assume unit element transfers and add dependent metadata costs separately.

evidence: Reviewed empty allocation, whole-allocation gap, zero-width gap, no-op movement, insertion at both ends, backspace at zero, forward delete at length, exact-capacity growth, and maximum arithmetic.

Reviewed overlap direction, self-aliasing insertion, resource-owning elements, partial transfer/construction failure, raw observers, serialization, residual deleted data, I/O failure, and snapshot lifetime.

Reviewed UTF-8 byte splits, scalar versus extended grapheme deletion, normalization choices, CRLF formation/splitting, marker affinity, distant alternating edits, multiple cursors, readers, and collaborative replicas.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: High-stakes editor claims remain outside the finite representation evidence.

evidence: Checked 0<=g0<=g1<=C, h=g1-g0, n=C-h, and exact live prefix-plus-suffix abstraction at each demonstrated transition.
Checked that each movement reads a live source, writes a gap destination, preserves order, holds gap width constant, and leaves the old source non-live.
Checked that insert, deletion, growth, traversal, marker, and serialization contracts do not expose gap slots as logical elements.
invariant_checking.notes: The Python marker None is explicitly pedagogical and is not treated as a production sentinel requirement.

evidence: Reviewed left-movement loop invariant and decreasing measure g0-p, including right-to-left overlap order.
Reviewed right-movement loop invariant and decreasing measure p-g0, including left-to-right overlap order.
Reviewed insertion/deletion abstraction equations and growth obligations for checked capacity, logical order, ownership, exact cleanup, and commit.
proof_review.notes: The proof is representation-level and conditional on the language's valid element-transfer and failure primitives.

evidence: The chapter states model assumptions for complexity and marks the executable result as a finite trace.

Unicode, performance, erasure, concurrency, collaboration, safety, and deployment conclusions are framed as contracts or additional evidence obligations rather than proven properties of one gap buffer.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: No benchmark, source review, or finite execution is represented as a universal theorem.

evidence: The standard-library Python snippet passed exact eight-line stdout, empty stderr, and zero exit status under recorded Python 3.14.4.
The trace emits evidence=finite_gap_trace, and all ten cited destinations plus all local links were checked directly.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: No production Emacs, piece tree, rope, generic object transfer, allocation failure, Unicode editor, concurrent reader, benchmark, secure erasure, or high-stakes workflow was empirically evaluated.

conceptual_review.notes: Reviewed abstract/physical mapping, directional movement, insertion/deletion/growth, locality-sensitive cost, traversal/invalidation, markers, derived indexes, Unicode units, normalization, serialization, remanence, undo, persistence, concurrency, multiple cursors, collaboration, testing, and structure alternatives.

practitioner_review.notes: Reviewed checked sizing, overlap-safe movement, generic lifetime, aliasing input, failure rollback, raw-view invalidation, marker affinity, line-ending updates, change intervals, two-span I/O, residual copies, snapshots, locking, realistic trace metrics, deterministic regressions, and operational evidence boundaries.

pedagogical_review.notes: Builds from fixed and dynamic arrays, derives the representation before implementation, provides a reproduced state machine, counters sixteen misconceptions, distinguishes Unicode layers, compares six structural families, and supplies ten distinct examples plus five progressively transferring exercises with complete matched answers. The requested legacy archive was searched but contained no gap-buffer course material to reuse.

limitations: Internal authoring, source, mathematical, executable-snippet, conceptual, practitioner, and pedagogical evidence only; no external Emacs or editor maintainer, language/runtime, Unicode, security, privacy, clinical, medical, safety, accessibility, human-factors, quality, regulatory, legal, operations, or independent academic review is claimed. The chapter and finite trace prove neither arbitrary implementation correctness, generic relocation safety, address stability, Unicode user expectation, race freedom, collaborative convergence, crash-safe persistence, secure erasure, hard latency, clinical correctness, certification, nor deployment fitness.
